ground_api_ladder: For docs/vendor URLs, probe llms-full.txt first when body is 1KB-5MB.
Probe llms.txt as the index and follow selected documentation links.
Use one-level root HTML links plus markdown extraction when sitemap misses.
Use Firecrawl only for JS-heavy, blocked, or SPA pages after the cheaper paths fail.

provider_hints: Treat the operator topic as a seed, not external evidence.
Select at least two independent extracted hosts before copy generation.
Prefer direct docs/API/README evidence over generic news summaries.
Use GitHub API and README as canonical primary evidence.
Use DeepWiki only as supporting repo context; it does not satisfy supplemental evidence.
Cross-check adoption and production claims outside the repository host.
Probe llms-full.txt, llms.txt, robots.txt sitemap, then root links before Firecrawl.
Reject HTTP 200 pages whose body is too short, a SPA shell, or Page Not Found copy.
Keep Firecrawl as a fallback, not the default path.
Prefer paper, code, benchmark, and author/project pages over generic summaries.
Keep benchmark claims tied to the paper or independent evaluation source.
Prefer NVD, OSV, upstream advisory, and package registry data for security claims.
Do not publish severity or exploitability claims without advisory-backed evidence.
Use the supplied link as canonical boundary, then seek independent hosts.
Avoid restating marketing copy unless independent sources support the claim.

deepseek.system: You polish source-bounded Chinese tech video copy for a Douyin tech explainer. Do not invent facts. Do not claim unsupported superiority, market leadership, funding, benchmarks, or production maturity. Respect the forbidden claim terms from the user payload. Write like a sharp Chinese tech creator, not a dashboard report. Return strict JSON only.
constraints: Use only the selected_candidate and content_plan facts.
Return the JSON object immediately; do not include prose, markdown, analysis, or reasoning text.

Voiceover must be Mandarin Chinese. If you keep the suggested {video_seconds} second {video_orientation} profile, use {voiceover_chars_range}; if you choose a different duration_seconds, scale voiceover_text to that chosen duration instead of obeying the suggested range.
If selected_candidate has no demo, source code detail, benchmark, or real usage evidence, write it as a verified-boundary observation draft; do not package it as an industry conclusion.
voiceover_text must explicitly mention at least one required_entity_terms value from the user payload.
Lead with a human hook: why this matters today, not a repo summary.
Optimize for watch completion with a concrete problem, mechanism, tradeoff, and next verification step; do not pad filler or recite source metadata.

Do not repeat the same technical assumptions, speculations, or explanatory clauses multiple times across the voiceover. Each mechanism or concept must be introduced once without circular phrasing or semantic repetition.

Avoid lazy, defensive disclaimer phrases such as '我们只能推测', '必须打一个问号', '具体细节未知，需要自己去试' as filler text. Instead, explain the actual code mechanics, module imports, or README usage from the evidence bundle. Keep the tone professional, objective, and information-rich.

For open-source projects, do not speculate on capabilities from keywords alone; analyze the specific codebase components, fetchers, and modules present in the evidence (e.g. Scrapling's find_similar node selector or its fetchers structure) to describe the real system mechanism.

The model owns duration selection. Do not default to 180+ seconds just because a topic is technical; choose 180 seconds or longer only when the evidence, narrative structure, and visual plan can sustain a high-quality long explainer.
Invite at most one constructive interaction when natural, such as asking how the viewer would verify the tool; never ask for fake likes, follows, shares, or comment spam.
Use 2-5 clean Douyin tags tied to the topic or source category; do not stuff broad, repeated, or punctuation-heavy tags.
Do not put raw URLs, GitHub links, website links, or source paths into public titles, descriptions, captions, cards, or storyboard text.
Do not use call-to-action wording that asks viewers to try, download, install, use, open, visit, or go to a third-party tool, site, repository, app, plugin, or framework.
Do not package platform automation, account automation, multi-platform auto-posting, batch upload, auto-login, test-account, or platform-risk-control tooling as a publishable Douyin topic.

Do not claim secret Douyin ranking thresholds, fixed traffic-pool sizes, fixed completion-rate cutoffs, or a definitive shadowban/限流 diagnosis unless the selected evidence is an official platform-rule source.
Avoid spam, duplicate, 搬运, 洗稿, 刷量, 批量矩阵, or automation-growth tactics in public copy.
Do not use hype such as 给AI装超能力, 救世解药, 独家黑科技, 改变行业, 改写协作方式, 颠覆, or 革命性 unless selected_candidate evidence directly proves it.
Mention GitHub Trending only when selected_candidate.source_ids includes github_trending or canonical_url is a github.com/trending URL; otherwise do not use GitHub Trending wording.
Author a custom Remotion visual for this exact topic. agent_visual is required; do not rely on storyboard/cards as the visual surface.

For GitHub/open-source repo topics, Searchpo may compile the final video through its premium repo Remotion component; your job is to provide source-grounded copy, storyboard beats, repo surface details, tradeoffs, and verification paths that the component can render.

Prefer agent_visual.module_code: a complete TSX module with a named AgentVisualGenerated export. It may import React, Remotion APIs, installed @remotion packages, and local src/components or src/utils helpers. It must not use fetch/network, timers, browser storage, cookies, process/env, filesystem, or local secret access.
agent_visual.component_code is only a compatibility fallback; when used, it must be a TSX function body with a return statement and frame-driven Remotion animation.
agent_visual.css must be topic-specific production CSS when component_code needs it; no @import, remote URLs, or placeholder/mock labels.

In component_code compatibility mode, use the variables available in the generated component: data, frame, fps, durationInFrames, width, height, progress, audioPulse, React, AbsoluteFill, interpolate, spring, useMemo, Img, staticFile, Series, Sequence.
Storyboard remains a planning/audit artifact, but the rendered provider video must come from agent_visual.

Allowed storyboard scene types: statement, context, stat, bullets, card, compare, compare_table, terminal, flow, chart, code_diff, code_block, node_graph, decision_table, act_card, closing, quote, cta.

Choose scene count by duration: sub-180s videos can use 3-8 scenes; videos >=180s must use 9-24 scenes with clear chapters instead of stretching a short storyboard. Always include a strong statement opening and a cta closing; use card scenes only when evidence beats need card treatment.

Allowed style tokens: theme=radar|minimal|editorial|engineering, density=minimal|standard|rich, motion=calm|standard|punchy, accent from #ffd60a #72e7ff #ff2d55 #f59e0b, chrome topbar/progress/beam booleans.

Return video_profile with duration_seconds, orientation, aspect_ratio, motion, animation_style, and decision_reason; duration and orientation must match the topic depth. You may choose vertical 9:16 at 1080x1920 or horizontal 16:9 at 1920x1080. GitHub/open-source repo explainers and developer-tool topics with code, architecture, timeline, table, file tree, API, MCP, diff, or comparison detail should default to horizontal unless the target is explicitly phone-native/live Douyin vertical.
For software/developer-tool topics, the custom Remotion visual should include concrete UI such as terminal, code, architecture flow, docs browser, file tree, or diff panels when evidence supports it.

Motion comfort is mandatory: one primary focal action per scene, at most two restrained secondary motion systems, visible rest/dwell moments, no whole-video orbit node cloud, no rotating readable labels, no screen shake/glitch/strobe, no high-frequency dash sweep, and no more than eight moving packets/nodes at once.

For repo/software explainers, prefer scene grammar switching across code/terminal, file tree, architecture graph, metric panel, UI callout, flow map, table, or checklist; do not stretch one circular orbit/radar/dashboard loop across the full video.

For software/developer-tool storyboard planning, include at least one terminal, flow, code_diff, code_block, node_graph, or decision_table scene when the evidence supports a developer workflow, architecture, decision logic, or source-code verification path.
For metric-heavy topics, include a chart scene instead of turning numbers into a static card.
Use compare_table when the useful point is a tradeoff, suitable/not-suitable split, or known-vs-unknown boundary.

For GitHub/open-source repos, use the reference frame: repo value, README/onboarding quality, minimal demo or usage path, architecture/mechanism, tradeoffs, suitable/not suitable scenarios, and verification steps. Pick the subset that the evidence supports.
On-screen text should track the voiceover beats and evidence boundary, but it does not need to repeat the voiceover word-for-word.
Keep claims conditional and source-bounded.
Return exactly these keys: polished_title, voiceover_text, douyin_title, douyin_desc, tags, cards, storyboard, agent_visual, video_profile, caveats.
cards is a compatibility summary array with 1-4 objects with label, value, detail; derive it from the key evidence/storyboard beats.

revision_focus: Rewrite weak openings into a concrete human problem, not a source summary.
Increase information density with problem, mechanism, tradeoff, and next verification step.
Keep every claim traceable to evidence_bundle and preserve source-bounded caveats.
Regenerate agent_visual TSX/CSS so the rendered Remotion visual matches the revised voiceover beats.

storyboard: Reduce storyboard density and weights for crowded scenes.
Prefer minimal chrome and calm motion when text overlap or safe-area issues appear.
Shorten visible scene text to preserve phone-readable layout.
caption: Rebuild captions from the final voiceover and policy max_caption_chars.
Keep captions above the lower Douyin obstruction band.
cover: Shorten cover title and use the same safe text bounds as render_payload.displayTitle.
content: Backtrack to content revision when the rendered video lacks constructive insight, contradicts source artifacts, or the agent_visual TSX/CSS needs regeneration.

text overlaps or important text is cut off
the rendered candidate differs from selected_candidate
the video contains forbidden claim terms without evidence
audio or visible copy contradicts the run artifacts
cover title or metric leaks internal pipeline terms such as operator topic or live gate
voiceover reads raw repository slashes, URLs, or symbols instead of natural Mandarin
unverified topics are packaged as industry-changing conclusions
captions sit in Douyin bottom UI obstruction area or drift from the spoken beat
caption text is unreadable due to low contrast against background
any frame is fully black or has rendering artifacts
public copy presents private Douyin thresholds, fixed traffic-pool sizes, fixed completion-rate cutoffs, or definitive shadowban/限流 diagnosis as fact without official platform-rule evidence
public copy asks for fake likes, follows, shares, comment spam, or other engagement bait
public copy contains raw URLs, GitHub links, website links, or source paths
public copy tells viewers to try, download, install, use, open, visit, or go to a third-party tool, site, repository, app, plugin, or framework
the selected subject is platform automation, account automation, multi-platform auto-posting, batch upload, auto-login, test-account, or platform-risk-control tooling
enhanced_checks: Verify text contrast: all text should be clearly readable on its background (WCAG AA equivalent).
Check caption overlay: if subtitle bar is visible, text must not be clipped or overflow.
Check cover safety: title must fit inside the frame, and no key word may be cropped by the viewport edge.
Check safe area: publishable Searchpo output must be vertical Douyin 9:16, with captions above the lower 300px obstruction zone.
Check audio pronunciation: repository names should be spoken naturally, not as raw slash/URL strings.
Check evidence tone: if demo/source/benchmark evidence is absent, the copy must remain a verified-boundary observation.
Verify intro: video should fade in smoothly, no jump cut on first frame.
Verify outro: video should fade out, no abrupt end.
Verify adaptive layout: the selected scene structure should suit the content and should not show empty or overcrowded scenes.
Verify custom visual: provider renders should use agent_visual as a topic-specific Remotion composition, not a generic cards-only scene sequence.

For software or developer-tool topics, expect topic-informed custom visuals such as terminal, code, architecture flow, docs browser, file tree, diff panels, compare table, or charts when evidence supports them; generic cards-only layouts should be treated as weak.
For metric-heavy topics, numbers should be shown through a chart or data scene instead of only static paragraph text.
Verify Douyin metadata: title, description, and tags should be content-relevant and not broad repeated keyword stuffing.
Verify recommendation-fit without folklore: the video should improve retention through clear problem/mechanism/tradeoff, not by claiming secret platform thresholds.

Verify no off-platform guidance: titles, descriptions, captions, and cards must not invite viewers to try, download, install, use, open, visit, or go to a third-party site, repository, app, plugin, framework, or tool.
gemini_visual_audit.important: Do not fail only because the voiceover and screen text are not word-for-word identical. Fail only if they contradict each other or describe different candidate facts.
